teaching_language.notes: Contrary to the initial 'bilingual / English track' hypothesis, this programme is fully English-taught. The official 2027/2028 programme page states 'Language: English', and all three third-year majors (Management, Finance, Economics) are flagged with the UK flag only - no Italian-flagged major exists in the study plan. Luiss lists 'Economics and Business' explicitly under 'Courses taught in English' on both the EU admission-test page and the non-EU certification page. The separate Italian-taught bachelor is 'Economics and Management' (Economia e Management), a different programme. Only the mandatory 4-ECTS 'Mandatory Language' credits may involve a language other than English.

academic_requirements.prior_qualification: A valid upper secondary school diploma granting access to Italian universities, held or obtained by the deadlines set by the University. For non-EU applicants: a secondary school diploma valid for admission to Italian universities, plus school report cards and a valid identity document or passport.
academic_requirements.minimum_curricular_requirements: Not applicable (bachelor-level programme; no ECTS/SSD curricular requirements). No subject-specific high-school curriculum requirement is published for Economics and Business.
academic_requirements.minimum_grade_or_gpa: No general minimum grade is published for the Luiss Test route. Country-specific minimum averages exist for qualification eligibility (e.g. Albania: Diplome e Matures Shtetrore with a minimum average grade of 6.5). For the non-EU certification route the thresholds are the test scores themselves (SAT 1200, LSAT 160, ACT 25, IB 36).
academic_requirements.country_specific_rules: Luiss publishes a country-by-country list ('Admission Requirements International Students') specifying which national qualifications are eligible and which recognition document is needed. Additional general rules: qualifications are accepted only if obtained after at least two years of attendance in the same school system; qualifications awarded within a mobility programme are not eligible; issuing and teaching institutions must both be accredited and recognised; professional/vocational qualifications are not eligible for Italian bachelor degrees; where the national system requires a national university entrance exam, the diploma is eligible only if accompanied by the certificate of successful completion of that exam.
academic_requirements.document_recognition: Depending on the country: a CIMEA Statement of Verification or Statement of Comparability, or an apostille of the diploma, or a Declaration of Value (DoV) issued by the competent Italian Embassy/Consulate. An 'attestation of qualification awarded' may be uploaded temporarily if the definitive documents are not yet available; enrolment stays pending until documents are delivered. Qualifications are verified only at the enrolment stage, not at admission - an admitted candidate whose qualification is later found non-compliant cannot enrol.
academic_requirements.compensatory_measures: If the qualification does not meet ministerial guidelines, the missing requirements can be made up with either: (a) completion of a Foundation Programme consistent with the intended field of study, lasting at least one academic year, issued by an accredited and recognised university; or (b) one full year of university/college studies at an accredited and recognised institution with all first-year exams passed. The compensatory qualification must be legalised and apostilled, or accompanied by a CIMEA Statement of Comparability. Luiss also offers its own Foundation Programme.

language_requirements.required_level: [uncertain] No English certificate level (e.g. B2) is published as a formal admission requirement for this bachelor programme for 2027/2028. English proficiency is effectively assessed by the fact that the admission test must be taken in English for English-taught courses. Luiss internally treats students enrolled in a fully English-taught degree as holding B2.4 by default.
language_requirements.accepted_certificates: [uncertain] No list of accepted English certificates (IELTS / TOEFL / Cambridge / Duolingo) with minimum scores is published for admission to this programme; such lists exist for the Luiss Foundation Programme (B2) and for master's-level routes, not for this bachelor's admission route. The full admission notice from October 2026 may add certificate requirements.
language_requirements.assessed_in_test: Indirectly: 'For degree courses taught in Italian, the test will be taken in Italian; for those taught in English, it will be taken in English.' Sitting the Luiss Test in English gives access to the English-taught programmes (including Economics and Business); sitting it in Italian restricts the candidate to Italian-taught programmes. The Luiss Test itself measures logical reasoning, problem-solving and mathematical skills rather than a separate English-language section.
language_requirements.exemptions: [uncertain] No formal exemption scheme is published, since no certificate requirement is published for this route. Students enrolled in a fully English-taught Luiss degree are automatically considered to hold level B2.4 for internal language-centre purposes.

entry_exam_or_test.test_name: Luiss Test (Luiss EU Test) for EU/Schengen applicants; for non-EU/Schengen applicants no Luiss-administered test - external certifications SAT, LSAT, ACT or IB are used instead
entry_exam_or_test.content: Luiss Test: psycho-aptitude questions inspired by the SAT model, assessing logical reasoning, problem-solving and mathematical skills. No separate English-language section is described. Preparation materials, simulations and exercises are available on a dedicated Luiss page.
entry_exam_or_test.format: Online, via the platform specified by the University, with fairness-control systems including asynchronous audio-video verification tools and live proctoring
entry_exam_or_test.dates: 2027/2028 first session: applications October 2026 - 10 February 2027; test administration 22-26 February 2027; registration by 4 May 2027. Two sessions are planned for 2027/2028; the second session calendar is [uncertain] not yet published. Candidates may take the Luiss Test more than once within the relevant academic year's scheduled sessions.
entry_exam_or_test.fee: EUR 150 participation fee (same EUR 150 fee applies to the non-EU certification route)
entry_exam_or_test.language_of_test: The test is taken in the language of the chosen degree course: Italian for Italian-taught courses, English for English-taught courses. Because Economics and Business is an English-taught course, the test must be taken in English. Taking the test in English gives access to the English-taught programmes; taking it in Italian restricts access to Italian-taught programmes. [uncertain: the 2027/2028 pages describe the language rule per chosen course rather than explicitly stating that an English-language test also unlocks Italian-taught programmes]
entry_exam_or_test.interview: Non-EU certification route: 'any assessment interview' may be part of the Commission's evaluation (possible, not guaranteed). EU Luiss Test route: no interview is mentioned.

source_quotes.quote: The Luiss EU Test is one of the admission routes to the Bachelor's Degree and the Single-Cycle Master's Degree in Law, designed for candidates who are citizens of an EU or Schengen country.
To access the test, you must have completed your application and indicated your chosen degree course, which is binding for admission and potential enrolment.

Courses taught in Italian Courses taught in English Economics and Management Law (single-cycle degree) Political Science Business Administration Economics and Business Global Law Management and Artificial Intelligence Politics: Philosophy and Economics

The test takes place online via the platform specified by the University and includes control systems to ensure a fair selection process, such as asynchronous audio-video verification tools and live proctoring.

The annual tuition fee for enrolment in the first year of the Bachelor's Degree in Economics and Business for the 2027/2028 academic year is 15,000 EUR, payable in three instalments, in addition to the regional tax.

The Luiss Bachelor's Degree in Economics and Business, belonging to the L-33 degree class, offers an international and interdisciplinary education that combines economics, management, finance, law and quantitative methods.

uncertainty_notes: ACADEMIC YEAR: The official programme page carries the year badge '2027/2028' and quotes 2027/2028 tuition; the 2026/2027 cycle is closed (bachelor enrolment deadline was 22 July 2026). All primary data recorded here is 2027/2028. The 2026/2027 cycle is recorded only as archival enrolment deadlines. There is no live application cycle open as of the access date 2026-09-04.

NOTICE NOT YET PUBLISHED: Only preliminary calendars are published for 2027/2028. Both the EU test page and the non-EU certification page state that the full admission notice ('admission call') will be published from October 2026. Therefore required-documents lists, minimum scores/rankings, results dates and any language-certificate requirement may change.

BILINGUAL / ENGLISH-TRACK HYPOTHESIS NOT CONFIRMED: The task brief flagged this programme as bilingual with only some majors in English. This was checked directly against the official study plan and is NOT the case. The programme page states 'Language: English' and all three third-year majors (Management, Finance, Economics) carry the UK flag marker with no Italian-flag major present. Luiss also lists 'Economics and Business' under 'Courses taught in English' in both admission notices. The Italian-taught sibling programme is the separate bachelor 'Economics and Management' (Economia e Management). Residual uncertainty: individual elective courses and the 4-ECTS 'Mandatory Language' component are not language-flagged individually on the page.

SECOND LUISS TEST SESSION: The EU page states 'the Luiss Test will be held in two sessions' for 2027/2028 but publishes only the first session calendar. Dates for the second session are unknown. Likewise the non-EU page publishes only 'the first certification selection session', implying further sessions with unpublished dates.

LANGUAGE REQUIREMENTS: No English-language certificate requirement (level, accepted certificates, minimum scores, exemptions) is published for admission to this bachelor programme for 2027/2028. English competence is handled implicitly by requiring the Luiss Test to be sat in English for English-taught courses. Published Luiss B2/IELTS/TOEFL thresholds found elsewhere relate to the Foundation Programme, the Language Centre and master's/MBA routes, not to this bachelor admission route. Treated as uncertain rather than asserted.

TEST-LANGUAGE UNLOCK RULE: The task brief asserted that taking the Luiss Test in English unlocks BOTH English- and Italian-taught programmes while taking it in Italian restricts to Italian-taught programmes. The published 2027/2028 pages only state the narrower rule that the test is taken in the language of the chosen (single, binding) degree course. Since only one binding course is chosen at application time, the broader 'unlock' framing could not be verified on luiss.it and is flagged uncertain.

SUBJECT AREA GROUP / SECOND CHOICE: No second-choice mechanism or subject-area grouping (Economics vs Law-Political Science) is published for bachelor admission for 2027/2028; both routes describe exactly one binding programme choice. subject_area_group is therefore recorded as not applicable / uncertain.

CAMPUS BUILDING: The programme page does not name a specific campus building. Luiss's registered address is Viale Pola 12, Rome; economics and management teaching is commonly at Viale Romania 32, but this is not confirmed on the programme page.

VISA / UNIVERSITALY: The Luiss non-EU bachelor page mentions only the candidate's own responsibility to obtain a study visa. It does not describe the Universitaly pre-enrolment procedure or a visa timeline, so visa_or_preenrolment_notes is only partially sourced.

SOURCE CONFLICT (minor): The Luiss Undergraduate School landing page (https://www.luiss.it/en/courses-and-masters-programmes/undergraduate-school) renders as a generic overview mentioning only 'three-year and single-cycle bachelor's degree programs in Law' when fetched, and does not enumerate programmes with per-programme language flags. The per-programme language mapping was therefore taken from the individual programme page and from the two admission-notice pages, which agree with each other.

404 PAGE: https://www.luiss.it/en/orientation-and-admissions/admission-procedures/admission-to-bachelor%27s-degrees-and-the-single-cycle-law-degree (the parent path of the non-EU certification page) returns HTTP 404; the child page itself returns HTTP 200 and was used. Note the odd Luiss URL structure where general bachelor admission pages sit under a path segment named '...-degree-programs-law'.

RESULTS DATES: Neither route publishes an explicit results-publication date for 2027/2028; both defer to 'the schedule set for the admission session' in the forthcoming notice.
MINIMUM SCORE FOR LUISS TEST: No pass mark or minimum score for the Luiss Test is published; the selection mechanics (ranking, quota, threshold) will appear in the October 2026 notice.
